newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end up reversing early losses.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end up reversing early losses.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly higher on Monday recovering early losses with traders saying that the bullish trend was expected to continue.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 0.19 percent, or 0.55 points, to 292.63 on a very high all-share turnover of 260 million shekels against 265 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.21 percent higher at 300.71.
Traders said that the session opened with a mild decline of 0.5 percent but during the day the market recovered.
"This is a real madhouse," said Danny Scharia at Capital Securities. "In the long run the market will continue to rise but we need a technical correction".
Scharia said that the Maof might fall to 290 before it starts rising again.

"The market continues to show strength and volume is very high which is the best indicator for the market's recovery. The market is emerging out of a crisis that lasted three years and I believe that the next two years will be very good," said Jacques Goldhar head of international activities at Jerusalem Capital Markets.

He added that despite the fact that the market rose sharply since May there is no indication for a correction. "The fact that millions of shekels flow into mutual funds shows that the positive trend will continue in the future".

Goldhar said that expectations for a rate cut also support the positive momentum. "Interest rates are still high and I believe that in the coming months the Bank of Israel will continue to lower its key lending rate".
The base rate has been 13.9 percent since the end of February. The Bank of Israel is scheduled to announce July rates on June 23.

Israel Chemicals lost 0.5 percent to 430 agorot. Sahar Securities and Investments said in a report released on Monday that the company will see strong earnings growth over the next three years as the company's efficiency measures bear fruit.

The most active shares were Bank Leumi, which fell 0.75 percent to 542 agorot on turnover of 13.7 million shekels; Koor Industries, which gained 1.5 percent to 31,874 agorot on volume of 10.2 million shekels; and Agis Industries which gained 0.5 percent to 3,920 agorot on turnover of 7.3 million shekels.
Agis said on Sunday that Merrill Lynch had acquired 19 percent of the company for 200 million shekels for distribution to clients.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233 DMG SAS
